question.worked_solution:
First, we isolate the exponential term:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}\cdot {7}^{3x-1}+1 & >0 \\ \frac{1}{2}\cdot {7}^{3x-1} & >-1 \\ {7}^{3x-1} & >-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, recall that a positive number raised to any real power is always positive. Since $7>0,$ we have

$$
{7}^{3x-1}>0
$$

for every real value of $x.$

In particular, every value of ${7}^{3x-1}$ is greater than $-2.$ Therefore,

$$
{7}^{3x-1}>-2
$$

for all real values of $x.$

Hence, the original inequality is satisfied for all real numbers.
